react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological theme: perturbation of L-tyrosine catabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) identified Tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:map00350) as the top KEGG hit (FDR = 1.61 × 10⁻⁶, fold-enrichment = 335.7) and simultaneously surfaced a cluster of SMPDB disease pathways (Alkaptonuria SMP00169, Dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency SMP00498, MAO-A deficiency SMP00533, Tyrosinemia Type I SMP00218) all at FDR = 1.28 × 10⁻⁶. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00350 as the top hit (p = 6 × 10⁻⁴), with Phenylalanine and tyrosine biosynthesis (hsa00400) rank 2 (p = 0.018). Mummichog m/z-network analysis on the empirical-compound human_mfn graph returned 'Tyrosine metabolism' as the top MUMM pathway (p = 5.04 × 10⁻⁴) and 'Biopterin metabolism' rank 2 (p = 0.012), reflecting the co-enrichment of dihydrobiopterin (KEGG:C02953) alongside tyrosine-derived metabolites. The five driver compounds all map to the tyrosine degradation scaffold: L-tyrosine (KEGG:C00082) as the upstream entry point, homogentisic acid (KEGG:C00544) at the terminal aromatic step, tyramine (KEGG:C00483) via decarboxylation, dopamine (KEGG:C03758) via hydroxylation, and dihydrobiopterin (KEGG:C02953) as the tetrahydrobiopterin cofactor required for the aromatic-hydroxylase steps (TYH / TH, PAH). The shared pathway accommodates glycine (KEGG:C00037) through transamination cycling and uric acid (KEGG:C00366) through purine salvage cross-talk. Losartan (KEGG:C07072), N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG:C01074) and iron (KEGG:C14819) did not map to the tyrosine cluster, indicating selective signal from the aromatic amino acid branch. The convergence of ORA (two tools) and m/z-direct network enrichment on the same pathway, with four verified driver metabolites each confirmed in the hit-rosters, constitutes a high-confidence multi-paradigm finding.
